title: DxSale — Liquidity Locker Ownership Backdoor Withdrawal Exploit Analysis
root_cause: Locker contract ownership was transferred to the attacker (verified `transferOwnership()` call, §8.1) at the moment reflected in the source-list incident timestamp; the new owner then called `setFee` to reduce the unlock fee to 1 wei and backdated lock `unlockTime` values to ~68 seconds after the Unix epoch (Jan 1970) so every position appeared immediately withdrawable, enabling the batch drain of all locked LP positions **three days later** (verified batch-drain window, §8.1). Public reporting's "~269 days prior, laundered through ~80 wallet hops" framing describes an earlier stage of the ownership chain that this report cannot independently confirm on-chain.
attack_tx: **7 verified real transactions** (§8.1) — the source list's provided hash `0x2b39f048033a9205c5a62ca43016263cfcca9bab74c48fdc06f43bd29307b26a` was not found on-chain and appears to be a one-character variant of an unrelated exploit (Flooring Protocol `0xb139f048...`)
vulnerable_contract: 0xEb3a9C56d963b971d320f889bE2fb8B59853e449 — BscScan-labeled **"DxSale Network: Legacy Liquidity Locker"** — verified on-chain (§8.1); contradicts earlier reporting that no locker address was public
